title: Unwritten revelation by living voice; corruption; writing for stability; do not require the unwritten when Scripture is given
pass_a_gloss: XXIII. Unwritten is that by which divine things to be believed are signified by the word handed down with living voice. By living voice — namely either of God himself, or of angels, or of the holy fathers, prophets and Apostles — the word of God was once handed down. But by the carelessness of human beings and the malice of Satan it was multifariously corrupted and depraved. Whence God restored and strengthened the purity of his word by new revelations from time to time, and at last for the sake of greater stability and certainty also willed it to be committed to writings. But here a rule is to be noted: When written revelation has been given, the unwritten is not to be required rashly, or tyrannically forced upon others; against Coster, Enchiridion of controversies chapter 1, where he says Christ willed neither that his Church hang upon paper writings, nor that mysteries be committed to parchments. Bellarmine book 4 On the unwritten word of God chapter 3. See Sadeel, Whitaker, and Nigrinus on the papistic contempt of sacred Scripture — indeed Christ himself John 5:39 and 17, and Paul 2 Timothy 3:15-16.
pass_b_english: XXIII. Unwritten revelation is that by which the divine things we must believe are signified by the word handed down with a living voice. By living voice — of God himself, or of angels, or of the holy fathers, prophets, and Apostles — the word of God was once delivered. Human carelessness and Satan's malice corrupted and depraved it in many ways. So God restored and confirmed the purity of his word by fresh revelations from time to time, and at last, for greater stability and certainty, also willed it to be committed to writing.

Here a rule must be noted: once written revelation has been given, the unwritten is not to be demanded rashly, nor forced on others by tyranny — against Coster, Enchiridion of controversies, chapter 1, where he claims Christ willed neither that his Church hang on paper writings nor that mysteries be committed to parchments. See also Bellarmine, On the unwritten word of God, book 4, chapter 3; and Sadeel, Whitaker, and Nigrinus on the papistic contempt of sacred Scripture — indeed Christ himself ([[John 5:39 >> Bible:John 5:39]]; [[John 17 >> Bible:John 17]]) and Paul ([[2 Timothy 3:15 >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:15]]-[[2 Timothy 3:16 >> Bible:2 Timothy 3:16]]).
source_text:
XXIII. Non scripta est, qua res divinae credendae verbo viva voce tradito significantur.
Viva voce, nempe vel Dei ipsius, vel angelorum, vel sanctorum patrum, prophetarum & Apostolorum, verbum Dei olim traditum fuit. Incuria vero hominum & malitia Satanae multifariam corruptum depravatumque fuit. Unde Deus puritatem verbi sui novis subinde revelationibus instauravit, firmavit, & tandem majoris stabilitatis ac certitudinis gratia etiam scriptis mandari voluit. Est autem hic notanda regula: Data revelatione scripta, non-scripta non est requirenda temere, aut aliis tyrannice obtrudenda; contra Costerum enchirid. controvers. cap. 1. ubi Christus, ait, nec Ecclesiam suam a chartaceis scriptis pendere, nec membranis mysteria committere voluit. Bellarminum lib. 4. de verbo Dei non scripto cap. 3. Vide Sadeelem, Whitakerum & Nigrini papisticum sacrae Scripturae contemptum, imo ipsum Christum Joh. 5. 39. & 17. & Paulum 2. Tim. 3. 15. 16.
